A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLiCE framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and renamed or relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original A5 state-tracking experiments, regular-language evaluations, and SLiCE results on six UEA datasets, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports these empirical evaluations together with new A5 length-generalisation results and original timing and memory experiments.

M1.justification: The SLiCE architectures and parallel-scan framework are retained. The stated Log-ODE computation changes locally: the matrix-product order in v1 Eq. (29) is reversed in v2 Eq. (64). The new pseudocode and additional block descriptions primarily document existing machinery; they do not establish an architectural redesign.

E1.justification: The four regular-language tasks and six UEA datasets remain unchanged. v2 adds an A5 extrapolation scenario, testing sequences up to length 5120 after training on lengths 3–40, beyond v1's A5 evaluations at matched training and evaluation lengths.

E2.justification: S4D is newly evaluated on regular-language tasks in Table 2. Comparisons also expand to diagonal-dense SLiCE on A5 and additional existing SLiCE structures on UEA. The external UEA baselines now tabulated were already compared in v1's appendix Figure 5.

E3.justification: v2 adds an A5 extrapolation protocol with validation-based early stopping and controlled EigenWorms experiments varying scan chunks and Log-ODE intervals. Existing reported settings also change: A5 block-diagonal hidden dimension increases from 128 to 256, and regular-language DeltaProduct batch size changes from 128 to 256. UEA timing and memory measurements are explicitly repeated on an H100 instead of the RTX 4090.

E4.justification: Figure 1b adds A5 length-generalisation analysis, while Tables 6–7 isolate the effects of parallel scans and Log-ODE compression on runtime and memory. The retained rank/block-size analysis gains separate diagonal and Walsh–Hadamard hidden-size results. Conversely, v1's A5 parameter-count comparison and accompanying analysis are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report regular-language means and standard deviations over five runs and use uncertainty-bearing UEA entries. v2 introduces no new stated seed policy, repeated-run count, confidence interval, or significance-testing procedure; additional entries and changed deviations do not establish a statistical-method change.

E6.justification: Many results change. At A5 length 20, Figure 1 changes Mamba's required layers from four to three and DeltaProduct's from four to two. Table 2 changes rank-four DPLR's average from 71.8 to 85.1, tying diagonal-dense SLiCE. UEA block-diagonal average accuracy changes from 64.5 to 64.0. v2 also adds extrapolation, model-variant, and timing results; cross-version runtime differences involve changed hardware.

T1.justification: The central expressivity theorems remain, but Appendix A adds a worked parity impossibility/construction argument and formal S6, linear-attention, and vectorisation derivations. The Log-ODE appendix revises bracket signs and coefficient normalisation. The block-diagonal proof also changes its target bound from O(1) to O(N^-1/2), although its final bound remains O(b_N^-1/2).

C1.justification: The unifying-framework, maximal-expressivity, and approximately twentyfold training-speed claims remain. v2 refines the diagonal-model claim from S4 to S4D and changes the conclusion's regular-language leadership claim from two block-diagonal variants leading to one variant achieving joint-best performance, consistent with the revised DPLR results.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's finite-dimension and alternative-structure discussion, v2 explicitly addresses large-model scaling, GPU-kernel bottlenecks, oversampling sensitivity, and the inability to stack Log-SLiCE layers directly. It revises interpretations of DPLR and Walsh–Hadamard generalisation and adds explanations of the timing ablations, including the observed memory floor and reduced recurrence bottleneck.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 documents recurrent and parallel forward passes. Appendix A.3 newly describes skip connections and state-transition regularisation; Appendix D.3 specifies normalisation range, structure-specific parameters, log-signature scaling, and scan chunk size. These substantially expand reproducibility information, without establishing that every newly disclosed detail represents an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused context and citations for ParallelFlow, linear attention, signature methods, and S4D, replacing the earlier S4 reference. It explicitly distinguishes structured sparsity imposed at initialisation from pruning. The central positioning around efficient, expressive structured state transitions remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanatory introduction to LNCDEs and matrix-valued states, standardises structured-variant names as SLiCEs, and reorganises the appendices. Former Appendix C is incorporated into the expanded Appendix A, proofs move to B, and Log-ODE material moves to C. Limitations become a separate main-text section, with experimental interpretations also rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a two-panel display, and Table 1 gains Log-ODE complexity information. UEA reporting is reorganised into an expanded aggregate table and a separate per-dataset table; Figure 5 is redrawn. v2 adds Algorithm 1 and two timing tables, expands the sensitivity table, and removes the earlier parameter-count table. The graphical proof figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added A5 extrapolation and controlled timing analyses address gaps in v1's evidence about practical generalisation and efficiency. Pseudocode and explicit applicability limits also improve usability. These benefits are tempered by mathematical inconsistencies: v2's block-diagonal proof targets O(N^-1/2) but concludes only O(b_N^-1/2), and Eq. (67) does not reflect the interval normalisation newly introduced in Eq. (66). The net improvement is therefore qualified.
